newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Mid-West spot electricity prices retreat.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Mid-West spot electricity prices retreat.

text.p: U.S. Mid-West wholesale electricity prices were mostly lower Monday, retreating along with spot natural gas prices to the tune of warmer weather and generation unit resumptions, brokers and marketers said.
"We came off hard today," said one Mid-West trader, referring mostly to next-day power prices.

Some generation units were returning from maintenance, including TVA Nuclear's 1,148 megawatt Sequoyah nuclear unit 2 in Tennessee, and Commonwealth Edison's 789 megawatt Quad Cities nuclear power unit 2 in Illinois.
Deferred Mid-West prices for December, and January/February held strength however, as traders looked for heavier demand during the cold winter months.
"The reality of the cold has started to dawn on people," one trader said.

Peak, non-firm electricity prices in the East Central Area Reliability Coordination Agreement (ECAR) were lower for Tuesday delivery at $17.00-19.00 from a broad range of $20.00-26.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) discussed late last week.
Off-peak next-day ECAR power was assessed little changed at $12.50-14.00 for Tuesday delivery.
Peak ECAR power for December was pegged relatively steady at $19.35-19.75, the brokers and marketers said.
January/February was talked at $21.40-21.80 per MWh.
In the Mid-Continent Area Power Pool (MAPP), peak non-firm power for Tuesday delivery was talked lower at $17.00-19.00 with little business done from $19.00-21.00 late last week, the sources said.
Off-peak non-firm MAPP power was said to have held steady at $9.00-10.00 per MWh.
In the Mid-American Interpool Network (MAIN), non-firm peak power was talked lower at $21.00-24.00 in the north and $19.00-21.00 in the south, the sources said.
Spot MAIN power was talked at $23.00-26.50 in the north and $18.50-21.00 per MWh in the south late last week.
Off-peak next day MAIN power was pegged steady at $12.00-14.00 per MWh.
Peak non-firm next-day power prices in the Southwest Power Pool (SPP) were talked at $23.00-26.00 in the north and $21.00-22.50 in the south, the sources said.
Next-day power was pegged in the $24.00-27.00 range for the entire region late last week.
Off-peak prices throughout SPP were reported to be steady at $12.00-14.00, the sources said.
Peak December SPP power was said to be talked steady at $21.85-22.05, while January/February was discussed near $22.90 per MWh, the sources said.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
